Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing a national digital identity system, including foundational ID systems that enable authentication across multiple services. Fully deployed means operational nationwide and accepting new registrations.
Comments: DRC has a partially deployed digital ID system. ONIP (Office National d'Identification de la Population) is the government agency responsible for population identification. Physical biometric national ID cards were piloted in 2022 (approx. 700 cards in Kinshasa) and formally launched in July 2023. The $1.2B contract with Afritech/IDEMIA was cancelled in August 2024. A new PPP agreement was signed with Singaporean firm Trident Digital Tech in June 2025 for the DRCPass digital ID system; phased deployment is underway as of August 2025 but nationwide rollout is not yet complete. No national ID cards had been issued since the 1990s (then-Zaire era) until the 2022 pilot.

revision_notes: All five original sources verified as live and relevant, but events have moved on: RDC-Pass was officially launched nationally on 13 June 2026 under a 20-year, $97.1m PPP with Trident Digital Tech (Biometric Update and Ecofin Agency, June 2026; Trident press release), and the platform is now online at rdcpass.gouv.cd, though as of that date citizen enrolment had only just begun (agent certification phase complete, mass registration starting roughly a week later) with wider national deployment still phased. Separately, ONIP announced in May 2026 the start of a second national population/ID-card identification exercise via a new PPP after the 2024 Afritech contract collapse. Because universal nationwide registration is still not complete, 'Partially deployed' (4) remains the best-supported code — confirmed, not changed, but comments/sources should be refreshed to reflect the June 2026 national launch.

Definition: Whether non-nationals including refugees, asylum seekers, and permanent residents are eligible to register
Comments: Some non-nationals are eligible. Refugees are mentioned as a targeted group for administrative registration under the ONIP scheme. DRC hosts significant refugee populations. The Bankable Africa report references 'targeted categorization of groups such as students, military personnel, Congolese abroad, and refugees.' No formal universal eligibility for all non-nationals has been established. The DRCPass system's documentation focuses on Congolese citizens.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Corroborated with a UNHCR Regional Protection and Return Framework report (2024) and a November 2024 ONIP-CNR memorandum of understanding, both confirming ONIP has integrated refugee/stateless indicators into its population identification questionnaire and is building a data-sharing framework with the National Commission for Refugees (CNR) for refugee identification. However, only around 16% of registered refugees held a CNR-issued refugee ID card as of 2022-2024, and there is no universal eligibility for all non-national categories. 'Some' (2) is confirmed, now on stronger authoritative sourcing beyond the single original news article.
